data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate recorded a material prior-year strengthening at gross level, driven primarily by reassessments in long-tail liability classes. Using the gross claims development triangle, prior-year (pre-2019/2020) reserves strengthened by approximately $130.2m (12.9% of opening gross claims outstanding). Management attribute the strengthening largely to an extensive review of older case files and a series of adverse US court rulings which required back-year reserve increases (notably in professional indemnity/financial institution and related liability classes). Separately, 2020 current-year claims were also affected by COVID-19 and US hurricane activity, but those impacts are largely current-year rather than prior-year reserve movements.
raw_causal_phrases: the need to strengthen back year reserves in certain long tail classes.

the combination of an extensive review of old case files by the newly strengthened team of in-house claims experts, and a series of unexpected adverse US court rulings, contributed a further $53m of losses and 11% to the combined ratio.
COVID-19 had a full year impact of $29m adding 6% to the combined ratio.
data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year gross reserve movement was not stated explicitly as a single gross figure. A gross prior-year movement was calculated from the published gross claims development (incurred) triangle (pages 34-35). The report also contains net prior-year deterioration figures (e.g. a net deterioration of $53.04m) and references to reserve strengthening of $53m related to specific liability classes; the triangle-derived gross strengthening (~$130.209m) differs from the quoted net figures. There is potential distortion risk from Part VII transfers / Reinsurance to Close references noted in the report which may affect comparability of development by underwriting year. Figures are expressed in the report's native currency (USD).
